This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT at Bidar (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.138/2016, vide judgment and award dated 04.11.2017.
2. The claimants are the parents of deceased Shanker, a one year old boy, who died in a road traffic accident on 24.01.2016.
He was run over by a tractor and he died at the spot.
A claim petition was filed by the claimants seeking compensation of a sum of Rs.11,51,000/-.

3. The insurer contested the claim petition denying the accident and contended that there was negligence on NC: 2023:KHC-K:1243 the part of the parents of the deceased in allowing him to play on the road and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor.
It also contended that the driver of the tractor did not possess a valid licence to drive the tractor and therefore, there was violation of the conditions of the policy.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P8.
The insurer did not lead any evidence and did not produce any document.

5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Meena vs. Rani Ammal in Special Leave to Appeal No.3464/2015 dated 15.02.2017 and held that the age of the parent should be considered for application of the multiplier.

It also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation Ltd., vs. Trilok Chandra NC: 2023:KHC-K:1243 reported in (1996) 4 SCC 362 and applying the multiplier as per the Schedule-II appended to the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.3,000/- per month, awarded a Nagendra And Anr vs Deelip And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110959681/
2 sum of Rs.45,000/- as loss of dependency and a sum of Rs.10,000/- to each of the claimants towards loss of love and affection and a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.20,000/-
towards funeral expenses.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal and Another vs. Lala and Others reported in (2014) 1 SCC 244 was considering a case of a death of boy aged 9 years who died in a road accident and though the deceased was not an earning member,
yet the annual income was considered at Rs.30,000/- and multiplier at 15 and determined the loss of dependency at Rs.4,50,000/- and awarded Rs.50,000/- towards loss of love and affection and other heads.

sentences.text:
He submitted that the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1243 judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra) was rendered in the year 2014 while the accident in the present case happened in the year 2016 and therefore, considering the cost of escalation, the compensation may be awarded.
7.

The learned counsel for the respondent/insurer on the other hand contended that the deceased was a one year old boy and therefore, the notional annual income had to be considered as per Schedule-II as prescribed under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

He submitted that due to the vagaries of life, the deceased could or could not have lived longer life and hence the assessment of notional income and the multiplier at 15 is just and proper and does not call for any interference.
8. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.

9. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellant, the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal NC: 2023:KHC-K:1243 (supra) while considering a case of death of a minor boy aged 10 years, who was not an earning member had considered his notional income at Rs.30,000/- and the multiplier was considered at 14.
If the same yardstick is applied to this case, the notional annual income deserves to be escalated taking into account the rate of inflation at 6%.
Therefore, the notional income in the year 2016 must be considered at a sum of Rs.33,600/-.
In view of the law declared by the Apex Court, the age of the deceased has to be considered for the purpose of determining the compensation and not the age of the parent.
The maximum multiplier of 18 deserves to be applied.
Consequently, the enhanced compensation to which the claimants are entitled to is re

- determined as follows:
Loss of dependency Rs.6,04,800/-
(Rs.33,600x18)
Loss of love and affection to each Rs.80,000/- of the claimant at Rs.40,000/-
Loss of estate and funeral Rs.33,000/-
expenses Total Rs.7,17,800/-

In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.95,000/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.7,17,800/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.6,22,800/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimants in equal portion, in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
